review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ἐγένετο γογγυσμὸς τῶν Ἑλληνιστῶν πρὸς τοὺς Ἑβραίους, ὅτι παρεθεωροῦντο ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ τῇ καθημερινῇ αἱ χῆραι αὐτῶν.
6:1.targetText: In those days when the disciples were increasing in number, the Grecian Jews among them began to grumble against the Hebraic Jews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.

groups.note: The genitive absolute πληθυνόντων ("multiplying") is rendered as a when-clause.
ἐγένετο γογγυσμός ("a grumbling arose") is rendered began to grumble.
Ἑλληνισταί are Greek-speaking Jews.
διακονία ("service") here is the daily distribution of food.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ here.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds that the Grecian Jews were among the disciples.

6:2.sourceText: προσκαλεσάμενοι δὲ οἱ δώδεκα τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπαν Οὐκ ἀρεστόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς καταλείψαντας τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ διακονεῖν τραπέζαις.
6:2.targetText: So the Twelve summoned all the disciples and said, “It is unacceptable for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.

groups.note: τὸ πλῆθος ("the multitude") of the disciples is rendered all the disciples.
οὐκ ἀρεστόν ("not pleasing") is rendered by the one word unacceptable.
The participle καταλείψαντας ("having left") is rendered as the infinitive to neglect.
BSB renders the infinitive διακονεῖν ("to serve") as purpose.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle προσκαλεσάμενοι, rendered summoned, to the main verb said.

6:3.sourceText: ἐπισκέψασθε δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἄνδρας ἐξ ὑμῶν μαρτυρουμένους ἑπτὰ πλήρεις Πνεύματος καὶ σοφίας, οὓς καταστήσομεν ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ταύτης·
6:3.targetText: Therefore, brothers, select from among you seven men confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will appoint this responsibility to them

groups.note: δέ is rendered Therefore, drawing the conclusion from verse 2.
μαρτυρουμένους ("being attested") is rendered confirmed.
The relative οὕς ("whom") is rendered them; BSB makes the responsibility the object of appoint.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB makes the responsibility the object of appoint, so ἐπί ("over") has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula between confirmed and full.

6:4.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ διακονίᾳ τοῦ λόγου προσκαρτερήσομεν.
6:4.targetText: and will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB continues the We of verse 3 and does not repeat the emphatic pronoun ἡμεῖς ("we").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:5.sourceText: καὶ ἤρεσεν ὁ λόγος ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους, καὶ ἐξελέξαντο Στέφανον, ἄνδρα πλήρη πίστεως καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου, καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Πρόχορον καὶ Νικάνορα καὶ Τίμωνα καὶ Παρμενᾶν καὶ Νικόλαον προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα,
6:5.targetText: This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, as well as Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.

groups.note: The article ὁ points back to the proposal and is rendered This.
Same word in a different form in BSB's Greek text; the meaning is the same.
προσήλυτος ("proselyte") is a convert to Judaism.
Ἀντιοχέα ("Antiochene") is rendered from Antioch.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts the verse without rendering καί.
BSB makes the group the object of pleased, so ἐνώπιον ("before") has no English word.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
BSB lists the names with commas; these καί have no separate word.

6:6.sourceText: οὓς ἔστησαν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀποστόλων, καὶ προσευξάμενοι ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας.
6:6.targetText: They presented these seven to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.

groups.note: The relative οὕς ("whom") is rendered these.
ἐνώπιον ("before") is rendered to after presented.
BSB turns this καί clause into a relative clause; the apostles are the subject.
The article τάς serves as the possessive.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB names the number of the men chosen in verse 5; the Greek has only the relative οὕς.
English joins the participle προσευξάμενοι, rendered prayed, to the main verb laid.

6:7.sourceText: Καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ηὔξανεν, καὶ ἐπληθύνετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν μαθητῶν ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ σφόδρα, πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει.
6:7.targetText: So the word of God continued to spread. The number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly, and a great number of priests became obedient to the faith.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

6:8.sourceText: Στέφανος δὲ πλήρης χάριτος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐποίει τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
6:8.targetText: Now Stephen, who was full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the description a relative clause with a supplied copula.

6:9.sourceText: ἀνέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς λεγομένης Λιβερτίνων καὶ Κυρηναίων καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων καὶ τῶν ἀπὸ Κιλικίας καὶ Ἀσίας συνζητοῦντες τῷ Στεφάνῳ,
6:9.targetText: But resistance arose from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, including Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and men from the provinces of Cilicia and Asia. They began to argue with Stephen,

groups.note: ἀνέστησαν ("rose up") is rendered resistance arose.
The article with the participle λεγομένης ("the one called") is rendered what was called.
Λιβερτίνων ("Libertines", freed slaves) is rendered Freedmen.
BSB renders this καί as including, counting the following groups with that synagogue.
The article τῶν ("those") stands as a noun here and is rendered men.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text; BSB makes the participle ("disputing") a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB speaks of resistance arising and has no word for τινες τῶν ("some of those").
BSB lists the groups with a comma; this καί has no separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds that Cilicia and Asia were provinces.

6:10.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀντιστῆναι τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ τῷ Πνεύματι ᾧ ἐλάλει.
6:10.targetText: but they could not stand up to his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke.

groups.note: καί joins a contrasting result and is rendered but.
The article τῇ serves as the possessive.
After the negative, καί is rendered or.

6:11.sourceText: τότε ὑπέβαλον ἄνδρας λέγοντας ὅτι Ἀκηκόαμεν αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ῥήματα βλάσφημα εἰς Μωϋσῆν καὶ τὸν Θεόν·
6:11.targetText: Then they prompted some men to say, “We heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him") is rendered by the name.
The one εἰς governs both Moses and God; BSB repeats against.

unmappedSource.reason: ὅτι introduces the direct quotation and has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:12.sourceText: συνεκίνησάν τε τὸν λαὸν καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐπιστάντες συνήρπασαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἤγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον,
6:12.targetText: So they stirred up the people, elders, and scribes and confronted Stephen. They seized him and brought him before the Sanhedrin,

groups.note: The participle ἐπιστάντες ("coming upon") is rendered as a finite verb.
The one object αὐτόν serves both verbs; BSB repeats him.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB lists the groups with a comma; this καί has no separate word.
One English the serves the whole list; these articles have no distinct counterpart.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB names Stephen as the object of confronted; the Greek participle has no object.

6:13.sourceText: ἔστησάν τε μάρτυρας ψευδεῖς λέγοντας Ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος οὐ παύεται λαλῶν ῥήματα κατὰ τοῦ τόπου τοῦ ἁγίου καὶ τοῦ νόμου·
6:13.targetText: where they presented false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.

groups.note: BSB joins this clause to verse 12 with where in place of τε ("and").
The one κατά governs both place and law; BSB repeats against.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders λαλῶν ῥήματα ("speaking words") as speaking alone.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

6:14.sourceText: ἀκηκόαμεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος οὗτος καταλύσει τὸν τόπον τοῦτον καὶ ἀλλάξει τὰ ἔθη ἃ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν Μωϋσῆς.
6:14.targetText: For we have heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to us.”

groups.note: ὁ Ναζωραῖος ("the Nazarene") is rendered of Nazareth.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves οὗτος ("this") after the name untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:15.sourceText: καὶ ἀτενίσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ καθεζόμενοι ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶδον τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ πρόσωπον ἀγγέλου.
6:15.targetText: All who were sitting in the Sanhedrin looked intently at Stephen, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name.
The article with the participle καθεζόμενοι ("those sitting") is rendered who were sitting.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts the verse without rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀτενίσαντες, rendered looked intently, to the main verb saw.
English gives what they saw as a that-clause.
English supplies the copula; the Greek has only ὡσεί ("like").
